system.description: (Araneae ctenizidae urbs ) A traptor is an Awakened nocturnal trapdoor spider that is commonly found in southwest North America, Africa, east Australia, and Asia. Traptors take five years to mature; once mature, they are approximately 1.8 meters long and weigh 12.5 kilograms. The younger version typically is about half the size and weight. They are very aggressive, but their diet normally consists of stray animals or other wildlife that makes the city their home. Though rare, it is not unheard of for a wounded or starving traptor to attack a metahuman. These urban hunters will use a combination of silk threads and special sensory pads on their front legs to track their prey. Unlike their mundane version, they are unable to burrow, but they have adapted all the nooks, crannies, and crevasses of the city to meet these needs. They will hide within dumpsters, abandoned vehicles, or buildings. Wherever they are hiding, they build a camouflaged hinged door made from its silk and material from the surrounding area. The hinged doors can look like just about anything, such as window air-conditioning units, vehicle doors or hoods, and building doors.
